registered: 2026-10-22T21:30-04:00 (before any run; rce dim had not been built when this was written)
question: What is the Nerode index (spec 6.10 dim(P)) and the redundancy of real RCE programs? No corpus measurement of this quantity exists in the literature for any language.
unit: one program = one row in results/dimension.jsonl: file, states, bound_reached, behaviours, redundancy_bits, per-region bits, fuel
population: spec/examples/*.rce of openIE-dev/rce at the commit recorded in results/ (59 programs plus the three dimension examples, which are excluded from the summary because they were written to have known values)
rce-examples: every .rce under body/, data/, ecosystem/, hardware/ that rce check accepts
rce-stdlib lib/*.rce functions with a state region, if any
command: rce dim --json --fuel 100000 FILE, engine frozen at a tagged commit whose binary sha256 is recorded before the run
primary_metric: median and interquartile range of redundancy_bits over programs where bound_reached is false; share of programs where bound_reached is true

hypotheses.H0: At least half of the accepted example programs have redundancy_bits > 0.5: ordinary hand-written Forms carry state that changes no future output.
hypotheses.H1: Programs whose intent names a single observable (one emit site) have higher redundancy than programs with several emit sites, because unread state accumulates where outputs are few.
hypotheses.H2: The per-region report attributes at least 80% of a program's redundancy to one region when redundancy_bits > 1.

falsifier: If the median redundancy over bounded programs is below 0.1 bits, the claim that accidental state is common in small Forms is wrong at this scale and dim is a diagnostic for large programs only.
exclusions: programs rce check refuses; programs with no state region (commands); decided by rule before running
reporting: every row kept; bound_reached rows reported separately as lower bounds; Wilson 95% intervals on shares
labels: no energy claim; cpu_s per program recorded as est_j = cpu_s x 10 W, labeled estimate
